metadata.title: Sarochi · Interactive 3D apparel showroom
metadata.description: An interactive 3D apparel-showroom concept with spatial product browsing, source-backed galleries and an experimental prepared photographic appearance preview.

hero.title: Step into the collection.
hero.intro: A small boutique becomes a spatial interface. Explore the racks, move from a garment to its source gallery, and open an experimental photographic appearance preview.

live.title: From the room to the details.
live.description: Browse the live boutique or inspect the implementation. Purchasing continues on the official Sarochi product page.

screenshot.alt: Live Sarochi 3D boutique showing apparel racks, a mirror, seating and interactive navigation zones

showcase.title: A room, a product, a closer look.
showcase.description: These are captures of the working showroom. The prepared photographic preview explores appearance; it is not a measurement of physical fit.

gallery.title: Prepared photographic appearance preview

product.title: Spatial discovery. Familiar next steps.
product.description: The 3D scene gives apparel exploration a sense of place, then hands off to product information and the official store. It is a showroom concept, rather than a separate payment platform.

features.title: Navigable boutique
features.text: Five selectable zones connect the room to apparel racks and focused product browsing.

features.title: Source-backed product galleries
features.text: Product information leads to available source photography and the official product page for purchasing.

features.title: Experimental appearance preview
features.text: Prepared photographic apparel previews support garment selection and local pants-color changes. They do not promise exact sizing, drape or arbitrary human try-on.

features.title: Several ways to explore
features.text: The implementation includes keyboard and responsive controls, with a non-WebGL product-link fallback when the scene cannot render.

engineering.title: A scene connected to a product flow.
engineering.description: Next.js and React Three Fiber connect a Three.js boutique to structured catalog data, product panels and a bounded photographic-preview workflow.

notes.title: Bounded catalog adapter
notes.text: An allowlisted read adapter uses timeouts, response limits and short-lived caching. The upstream commerce backend remains the official store’s system.

notes.title: Keep exploration connected
notes.text: Scene selection, rack navigation, product information and the return from the appearance preview share a coherent product context.

notes.title: Clear preview boundaries
notes.text: Prepared previews are distinct from optional fresh generation. Exact-person garment reconstruction, physical fit and guaranteed generation availability are not claimed.
